context: We refer to the associated subsets of Q as Qei := Cie ∩ Q, i ∈ {1, . . . , k}, and Qvi := Civ ∩ Q, i ∈ {1, . . . , dC2(v) }, respectively. Since Q is odd, there is at least one i∗ ∈ {1, . . . , k} (i∗ ∈ {1, . . . , dC2(v) }) such that |Qei∗ | ≤ |Q| (|Qvi∗ | ≤ |Q|) is odd as well. Now either (Cie∗ , Qei∗ ) ((Civ∗ , Qvi∗ )) is simple in which case we are done. Or, we find an edge f ∈ Cie∗ , f = 6 e, that occurs more than once on Cie∗ (a vertex w = 6 v in Civ∗ such that dCiv∗ (w) > 2) and have thus reduced the extraction of a simple cycle to a strictly smaller non-simple one. Thus, since any simple cycle has length at least three, the according recursion must terminate after finitely many steps with a cycle that is simple. It however remains open how to extract a (chordless) simple odd closed walk from a non-simple one efficiently.
